answer: Sequential work registry: each identity must submit the next entry in a chained hash sequence whose difficulty is calibrated to a juniper-class benchmark, and entries are accepted only if their timing matches wall-clock hardware execution. The rule enforces that every new identity pays the full compute latency serially, so an attacker’s parallel clon army gets no speedup from forgery. A single orchard of fake identities costs the same total energy as one honest miner’s shale-grade rig, making mass registration economically flat rather than cheap.
